lawyer:
Dr. Rafique Rahman, Senior Advocate, instructed by Azra Ali, Advocate-on-Record. ------ For the Petitioner 
Mahbubey Alam, Senior Advocate, instructed by Chowdhury Md. Zahangir, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Respondent

full_judgment:
Mohammad Fazlul Karim J: The defendant No.5 petitioner seeks leave to appeal against the judgment and decree dated 10.01.2004 passed by the High Court Division in Appeal from Original Decree No. 29 of 1996 dismissing the appeal affirming those dated 3.9.1995 of the First Court of Subordinate Judge, Khulna in Title Suit No. 26 of 1992. 

 2. The plaintiff-respondent filed the suit impleading the petitioner as defendant No.5 and others as the defendants praying for decree declaring the deed of agreement between the parties cancelled and for recovery of compensation to the tune of Tk. 25 lac stating, inter alia, that in terms of Asian Development Bank Loan No. 329 Bangladesh Krishi Bank was entrusted to establish three Ice Plants in Bangladesh and in terms thereof the plaintiff decided to establish Ice Plant and Cold Storage on the supplying of the necessary machinery by the defendant No.5- Krishi Bank out of its fund and being approached the agreement No. 25 was executed on 15.06.1985 between the concerned parties including the plaintiff and the defendant No.5 and the plaintiff was granted sanction letter in 1985 on condition that the Krishi Bank would supply the machinery on payment of fund in foreign currency and the plaintiff would purchase land and construct factory building for establishment of the Ice Plant and cold storage. It was agreed upon that the loan would be sanctioned in foreign currency and not in Bangladeshi currency. A tripartite contract was entered into between M/s. Jain Enterprise on 16.5.1985 for supplying of machinery and other materials and in the said contract Frick Company of USA rep-resented by its local agent Messers Eastern Trading Agency Limited was the first party and in the 2nd agreement Covington Diesel of USA represented by local agent Messers Eastern Trading Company was the first party and in both the agreements 2nd and 3rd parties were Bangladesh Krishi Bank and the plaintiff's company respectively. The plaintiff in terms of the agreement deposited 10% of Letter of Credit margin with Bangladesh Krishi Bank, Labonchora Branch and also opened Letter of Credit on 18.6.1985 with the Principal Office of Janata Bank, Dilkusha Commercial Area. In terms of the first agreement it was decided that a compressor would be supplied to the plaintiff and as there were some mistakes committed by the Krishi Bank at the time of opening of the Letter of Credit the machinery had not been reached and the Letter of Credit stood can-celled and the plaintiff had no latches or inaction in the matter but it was caused due to negligence and mistake of the Krishi Bank which led the plaintiff to suffer irreparable loss and injury and also a loss of time of about 1½ years. Bangladesh Krishi Bank regretted not to supply the imported Compressor and the Generator and advised the plaintiff to import the Compressor and the Generator at his own initiative. Consequently, agreement was executed on 05.11.1986 for importing of the Compressor and the Generator and the first party to the said contract was Sunita Textile and Engineering, Calcutta represented by their local agent Kingsook Limited, Dhaka and for the 2nd agreement Ward Power Limited. Stamford, UK represented by its local agent Messers Kingsook Limited was the first party and in the said agreement 3rd and 4th parties were the plaintiff's company and the Bangladesh Krishi Bank respectively. In terms of the said agreement the plaintiff opened Letter of Credit with Janata Bank on 23.11.1986 of importing a Generator through Chittagong Port. It is further alleged that for the establishment of the project there was a tripartite contract executed between the concerned parties for supplying of other machinery and one Messers Jain Enterprise, Bombay represented by local agent M/s. Eastern Trading Limited was the first party and Bangladesh Krishi Bank and the plaintiff were the 2nd  party and 310 party respectively. In terms of the said agreement Air Blower and Amonia Gas along with 26 other items were to be sup-plied and the foreign currency for those materials were lying with the Krishi Bank and in terms of the advice of Krishi Bank the plaintiff opened Letter of Credit with Janata Bank on 18.6.1985 which was valid up to 31.12.1985 and the plaintiff deposited 10% of the Letter of Credit which was opened on 18.6.1985 in terms of the agreement No. 25. A portion of the machinery arrived at Benapol port but having several reminders Bangladesh Krishi Bank and insurance company did not make any inspection and also did not take any step to release the machinery which were lying at the Benapol port uncared for and ultimately the plaintiff had to release the said part machinery on payment of huge salami and demurrage on 27.10.1986. The supplier did not fulfill the contract in supplying the entire machinery and the 2nd installment of the machinery arrived at Benapol port on 09.5.1987 without Air Blower and Amonia Gas. The plaintiff further alleged that the defendant No.5 Bangladesh Krishi Bank has not yet arranged to import of Air Blower and Amonia Gas, without which the project in question, is not able to go into operation. The 2nd installment of the machinery were kept lying at Benopol port and the machinery were mostly damaged by woodworms and also destroyed by insects and the plaintiff got the said materials inspected through "The Finds" who did the inspection work from 19.9.1987 to 12.1.1987 and submitted their report on 19.10.1987. From the report it appears that Bombay office transmitted 82 packets of machinery but only 80 packets arrived at Benopol port and most of the machinery were infested by insects, woodworms and damaged causing unusable. The plaintiff wrote letter to the defendant No.5 and also submitted the aforesaid report to defendant No.5 on 26.10.1987 but without any result. In 1985 when the plaintiff took up the project for establishment of ice Plant and Cold Storage, there was huge demand for such plant and shortage in the country and the plaintiff could earn profit if project could go into operation in 1986-87 but due to latches and inaction of the defendant No.5 the project could not go into operation. The plaintiff subsequently applied for additional loan and asked the defendant No.5 to import Air Blower and Amonia Gas for the project but those were not attended to and meanwhile the project cost increased by 35%. Meanwhile, the plaintiff acquired .16½ decimals of land in commercial area and constructed a factory building and thereby invested about Tk.13,00,000/-. The plaintiff further requested the defendant No.5 for loan of Tk. 35,00,000/- and subsequently asked for at least Tk. 18,97.075/- but the defendant No.5 informed the plaintiff to apply in the relevant form to which the plaintiff submitted form on 12.12.1987 but the said prayer remained unattended. On the other hand, without supplying Air Blower and Amonia Gas and other necessary machinery defendant No.5 by letter dated 17.7.1988 wanted to know as to when the plaintiff would go in operation with the project and subsequently the then General Manager of the Krishi Bank made inspection of the factory building constructed by the plaintiff and assured the plaintiff with financial help but ultimately did nothing and at the time of approaching the plaintiff was asked to supply lay out plan to defendant No.5 by letter dated 15.8.1988 and the plaintiff accordingly deposited the lay out plan and other necessary documents on 29.8.1988 but the Krishi Bank did not take any action in the matter and ultimately the plaintiff sent a notice through his learned Advocate on 09.05.1989 to the District General Manager of Krishi Bank intimating clearly that, the non-supplying of Air Blower and Amonia Gas and for non-performance of other terms of the contract, the agreement between the parties stood cancelled and it was further intimated that for non-performance of the contract by the Krishi Bank the plaintiff is entitled to compensation of Tk. 25,00,000/- Thus, the correspondence continued between the parties and the defendant No.5 having done nothing the plaintiff was compelled to institute the suit. 

 4. The trial Court framed necessary issues and on consideration of the evidence on record came to the finding that the defendant no.5 did not perform his part of the contract by supplying all the machinery including Air Blower and Amonia Gas which were mandatory for commission of the project and thereby the plaintiff was put to sustain huge loss and injury and the contract in question is liable to be cancelled in terms of Sections 51 and 53 of the contract Act. The trial Court further considered the evidence and concluded that the plaintiff is entitled to compensation of Tk. 25,00,000/-. Accordingly, by judgment and decree dated 04.9.1995 the trial Court decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff with cost. 

 6. Dr. Rafiqur Rahman, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner submitted that both the Courts below failed to comprehend that admittedly there was a tripartite agreement and it was not disputed and the present petitioner as per contract opened the Letter of Credit for all equipment required for the implementation of the project of Ice Plant and it is also on record that the supplier M/s. Jain Enterprise, 1st Party failed to supply two items of the Letter of Credit namely 'Air Blower' and `Amonia Gas' and it is also on record that before releasing the shipment and making the payment of Letter of Credit the present petitioner sought permission from the plaintiff-respondent (Exhibit Nos. 36 and 37) and after obtaining their consent accepted the shipment and made payment thereon, which, in no way, came within the mischief of sections 51,53 and 54 of the Contract Act. The learned Counsel further submitted that the learned Courts below also failed to take notice that there is a tripartite agreement and the present petitioner is not the supplier but financier, who is only responsible to facilitate finance for necessary equipment for setting up an 'Ice Plant' and there is noting to show that the present petitioner did not supply necessary funds for purchasing the equipment, rather it is admitted in the plaint that "বাদীপক্ষ উক্ত মালামালের ব্যাপারে সম্পূর্ন অনভিজ্ঞ থাকায় ঐ সময় মালামাল বুঝিয়া পাইতে পারেন নাই তাছাড়া কাষ্টমের চাপের মুখে তাহারা উক্ত মালামালের কাগজপত্র না দেখেই সই করিতে বাধ্য হন। ১৯৮৫ ইং সালে যখন প্রকল্পটি হাতে নেওয়া হয় তখন আইস প্লান্ট ও স্টোরেজ এর চাহিদা দেশে ছিল। এবং ১৯৮৬-৮৭ সালের ভিতর উৎপাদনে যাইতে পারিলে উহার ফিজিবিলিটি এবং প্রকল্প হাতে নেওয়ার উদ্দেশ্য সফল হইত। এবং উহা একটি লাভজনক ব্যবসা হইত।" clearly shows that plaintiff's lack of knowledge prevented implementation of the contract and under apprehension of non-profitability, the plaintiff filed the suit and as such the Courts below erred in law in decreeing the suit. The learned Counsel lastly submitted that the Courts below have also failed to construe the impugned agreements in its true perspective and wrongly treated the petitioner as a supplier and applied Sections 51,53 and 54 of the Contract Act, and as such the impugned judgment and decree are liable to be set aside.
